title: Cap. VI Arg. 8 close: Vasquez split grace/glory fails — will to give the kingdom causes perseverance
pass_a_gloss: From this gift, specially prepared and given to certain ones, we gather that eternal life was antecedently destined for the same. Vasquez the Jesuit, convicted concerning this absolute and gratuitous predestination of certain persons to faith and perseverance, replies that it is most true that predestination to the having of grace does not depend from foresighted merits or our actions; but that election to the having of glory depends from those, and that this is the perpetual sentence of the Scriptures and of Augustine. But in vain does the Jesuit try to tear apart what Scripture and Augustine, the best interpreter of the Scriptures in this matter, taught to be most closely joined. For Scripture does not acknowledge another election or predestination to efficacious grace than that which is connected with that will of giving glory; which will, according to our mode of considering, is prior to the will of giving efficacious grace, and the cause and rule of the same. Hence we are said to be predestinated unto the adoption of sons, Eph. 1:5, which clearly denotes destination not only of grace, but of glory or the heavenly inheritance. So Christ speaking of the predestinated, Luke 12:32: Fear not, little flock, for it has pleased your Father to give you the kingdom. Where the will of giving the kingdom is brought as the peculiar cause of that providence which God exercises toward the elect, that he may keep them, and make them persevere notwithstanding dangers and temptations. The will therefore of giving glory, or election to life, is the reason why they persevere before others; not foresighted perseverance the reason why they were elected before others.
pass_b_english: From this gift specially prepared and given to some, we gather eternal life was already destined for them. Vasquez the Jesuit, pressed by this absolute gratuitous predestination of certain persons to faith and perseverance, answers: yes, predestination to grace does not hang on foresighted merits — but election to glory does, and that is the standing view of Scripture and Augustine. In vain he tries to split what Scripture and Augustine join most closely. Scripture knows no election to efficacious grace except what is tied to the will to give glory — which will, in our way of considering, is prior to the will to give efficacious grace, and its cause and rule. Hence we are predestined unto adoption as sons (Eph. 1:5) — destination of glory and the heavenly inheritance, not grace alone. So Christ to the predestined (Luke 12:32): Fear not, little flock, for it pleased your Father to give you the kingdom — the will to give the kingdom as the peculiar cause of the providence that keeps the elect and makes them persevere through dangers. The will to give glory (election to life) is why they persevere before others — not foresighted perseverance why they were elected before others.
source_text: Ab hoc dono, quibusdam specialiter praeparato et donato, nos colligimus, vitam aeternam fuisse iisdem antecedenter destinatam. Vasques Jesuita convictus de absoluta hac et gratuita certarum personarum ad fidem et perseverantiam praedestinatione, respondet, esse verissimum, praedestinationem ad habendam gratiam non dependere ex praevisis meritis aut actionibus nostris; sed electionem ad habendam gloriam ex illis dependere, atque hanc esse perpetuam Scripturarum et Augustini sententiam. Sed frustra conatur Jesuita divellere, quae Scriptura et Augustinus optimus hac in re Scripturarum interpres, docuit esse conjunctissima. Scriptura enim non agnoscit aliam electionem aut praedestinationem ad gratiam efficacem, quam quae connexa est cum ea voluntate dandi gloriam; quae voluntas, secundum nostrum considerandi modum, prior est voluntate dandi gratiam efficacem, et causa ac regula ejusdem. Hinc praedestinati dicimur in adoptionem filiorum, Ephes. i. 5. quae non modo gratiae, sed gloriae sive haereditatis caelestis destinationem perspicue denotat. Sic Christus loquens de praedestinatis, Luc. xii. 32. Nolite, inquit, timere, pusille grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum. Ubi voluntas dandi regnum affertur tanquam causa peculiaris ejus providentiae quam Deus exercet erga electos, ut eos custodiat, et non obstantibus periculis et tentationibus perseverare faciat. Voluntas ergo dandi gloriam, sive electio ad vitam, est ratio cur prae aliis perseverent; non praevisa perseverantia, ratio cur prae aliis electi fuerint.
